 These Criminal Petitions coming on for reporting
settlement this day, the Court made the following:-




 ORDER

Heard Shri Purushothaman K.N., learned advocate

for the petitioners in Crl.P. No.458/2018 and Shri Pradeep

Singh, learned advocate for the petitioner in Crl.P.

No.1632/2018 and Shri S. Rachaiah, learned HCGP for

respondent No.1-State in both petitions.

2. The first petitioner - Allwyn Jeetendra in Crl.P.

No.458/2018 is the husband and the second respondent is

his wife. Petitioners No.2 and 3 are the parents of the first

petitioner. The second respondent-wife initiated

proceedings in CC No.23097/2012 for the offence

punishable underSection 498Aof IPC and the first

petitioner-husband initiated proceedings in C.C.5CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018No.54217/2014 before the X Additional Chief Metropolitan

Magistrate, Bangalore, for the offences punishable underSections 323,324,504and506of IPC.

3. Learned advocates for the petitioners and 2nd

respondent jointly submit that the parties have settled

the matrimonial dispute amicably before the Bengaluru

Mediation Centre and filed a memorandum of settlement

in M.C. No.2764/2012. In terms thereof, parties have

agreed to cooperate for quashing of proceedings in

CC.No.23097/2012 and CC.No.54217/2014.

Accordingly, they have filed a memorandum of

compromise and a Joint Affidavit of even date, duly

signed by the parties and their respective advocates

with a prayer to quash the proceedings in

CC.No.23097/2012 and CC.No.54217/2014 both

pending on the file of X ACMM, Bengaluru. They pray

that this petition be disposed of in terms of the said

Joint Affidavits.

4. It is submitted by the learned advocate for the

petitioners that the first petitioner in Crl.P. No.458/2018 is

in Australia and therefore, he may be permitted to be

represented by his power agent. Accordingly, the first

petitioner is permitted to be represented by his father and

power agent, the third petitioner herein. The petitioners

No.2 and 3; and respondent No.2 are present and

identified by their respective advocates. They admit the

terms of settlement stated in the Joint Affidavits. The

same are lawful and hence accepted. The Joint Affidavits

read as under:

" JOINT AFFIDAVIT OF PETITIONERS 1, 2,3 AND RESPONDENT No.2 IN CRIMINALPETITON No.458/2018We, Allwyn Jeetendra Son of Bhaktha
 Prasad, aged 34 years, presently residing at
 Unit No.133, Junction Terrace, Annerley
 Queensland, Australia, permanent resident of
 No.402, 4th 'A' Cross, 4th Main, OMBR Layout,7CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018Bangalore-560 043, represented by GPA
 HOLDER T.Bhaktha Prasad 2) Christina
 Malini, W/o T.Bhaktha Prasad aged 65 years,
 residing at No.402, 4th 'A' Cross, 4th Main,
 OMBR Layout, Bangalore-560 043, 3)
 T.Bhaktha Prasad S/o Late Thevamani aged
 69 years, residing at No.402, 4th 'A' Cross, 4th
 Main, OMBR Layout, Bangalore-560 043, and

4) Ms.Jaquline Moras, Daughter of Late
 Mr.John Moras, aged 39 years, residing at
 Taccode house and Post Karkala Taluk,
 Mangalore District-574 197, do hereby
 solemnly affirm and state on oath as follows:-

1. We submit that petitioner No.1 is accused No.1
 in CC.No.23097/2012, in (Crime
 No.203/2011), wherein Charge sheet was filed
 by Respondent No.1 for the offence punishable
 underSections 498A,506and34of the Indian
 penal Code. Petitioner No.1 is the husband of
 Respondent No.2 and Son of Petitioners 2 & 3.

I, Petitioner No.1 is represented by GPA
 HOLDER T.Bhaktha Prasad, who is none other
 than my Father.

2. We submits that Petitioner No.2 is accused
 No.2 and none other than the Mother in law of
 Respondent No.28CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018

3. It is submitted that Petitioner No.3 is Accused
 No.3 and the Father in law of Respondent
 No.2.

4. The Respondent No.2 is the complainant before
 the Jurisdictional Police, the 1st Respondent.

5. We submit that Respondent No.2 herein had
 filed a complaint on 20/11/2011 in case
 bearing Crime No.203/2011 before the
 Ramamurthy Nagar Police Station, against the
 1st respondent herein, under the provisions ofSections 498A,506and34of IPC against the
 husband, Mother in law and the Father in law
 before the X ACMM at Bangalore based on
 which the charge sheet was filed against the
 petitioners 1 to 3.

6. It is submitted that Respondent No.2 had filed
 a Domestic Violence Case against the
 Petitioners 1 and 3 in MC No.07/2011. It is
 submitted that this bain the stat eof affairs
 Petitioner No.3, the Father in law of
 Respondent No.2 had filed a Writ Petition
 Nos.14529-14530/2015 challenging the orders
 passed in M.C.No.07/2011 pending on the file
 of Hon'ble JMFC (III Court).

7. It is submitted that during the pendency of the
 said Writ Petition Nos.14529-14530/2015, the9CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018matter was referred to the Bangalore Mediation
 Centre to enable the parties to arrive at a
 mutual settlement. Accordingly, the parties in
 the Writ Petition amicably resolved their
 dispute and entered into a Memorandum of
 Settlement underSection 89of CPC before the
 Bangalore Mediation Centre.

8. It is submitted that based on the said
 Memorandum of Settlement, this Hon'ble Court
 disposed of Writ Petition Nos.14529-
 14530/2015 (GM-FC) and directed the registry
 to dispatch the memorandum received from
 the Bangalore Mediation Centre to the I
 Additional Principal Judge, Family Court,
 Bengaluru, wherein M.C.No.2764/2012 was
 pending.

9. It is submitted that Petitioner No.1 herein had
 filed a Petition for Divorce underSection 10(x)of the Divorce Act against his wife, Respondent
 No.2 herein, in M.C.No.2764/2012 on the file
 of the I Additional Principal Judge Family Court
 at Bangalore.

10. It is submitted that this Divorce Petition was
 also referred to the Mediation Centre for
 resolution of the dispute as per the directions
 of this Hon'ble Court in W.P.Nos.14529-10CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/201814530/2015 and accordingly, the Parties to the
 Divorce Petition namely B.Alwyn Jeetendar
 Petitioner No.1 herein and Jaquline Moras,
 Respondent No.2 agreed to resolve their
 dispute through the mediation process and
 entered into a Memorandum of Settlement
 underSection 89of CPC read with Rules 24
 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure
 (Mediation) Rules 2005 in M.C.No.2764/2012.

11. It is submitted that based on the Memorandum
 of Settlement executed by the parties, the
 Hon'ble Family Court dissolved the marriage
 between Petitioner No.1 and Respondent
 herein and a Decree has been passed
 dissolving the said marriage.

12. It is submitted that in both the Memorandum
 of Settlement Agreement, the parties have
 agreed to cooperate for compounding the
 Criminal cases filed by the respective parties
 including CC.No.23097/2012 filed before the X
 ACMM, Bengaluru underSections 498Aand506of IPC.

13. It is respectfully submitted that the whole set
 of cases both civil and criminal have arisen
 from out of the marriage between the husband
 and wife, i.e. Petitioner No.1 and Respondent11CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018No.2 herein which has been amicably resolved
 and a Decree of Divorce has been granted by
 the I Additional Principal Judge Family Court
 Bangalore, and the parties have amicably
 agreed to compound the criminal cases filed
 against each other to put an end to the
 litigation.

14. It is respectfully submitted that no purpose
 would be met by allowing the criminal
 prosecution to continue in the above stated
 case, as we have agreed to put an end to the
 ill-fated unfortunate litigation.

15. We submit that we have voluntarily agreed to
 put an end to this litigation and there is no
 force, coercion or undue influence in execution
 of this Joint Affidavit.

16. I, Petitioner No.1 had agreed that I shall pay a
 permanent alimony of Rs.28,50,000/- (Rupees
 Twenty Eight Lakhs Fifty Thousand only). A
 sum of Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Lakhs
 only) has already paid in accordance to the
 Memorandum of Settlement agreement. The
 Balance amount of Rs.8,50,000/- (Rupees
 Eight Lakhs Fifty Thousand only) is paid today
 by demand draft bearing No.519079, dated12CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/201825/09/2018 drawn on Indian Bank, Dodda
Banaswadi, Bangalore.

We pray that this Hon'ble Court may be
pleased to allow the petition and Quash the
proceedings in CC.No.23097/2012 on the file
of the X Additional Chief Metropolitan
Magistrate, Bangalore and consequently Quash
the crime No.203/2011 before the
Ramamurthy Nagar Police Station, K.R.Puram
Sub Division, Bangalore, in the interest of
justice and equity."

" JOINT AFFIDAVIT OF PETITIONER AND
RESPONDENT NO.2 IN CRIMINALPETITION No.1632/2018We, 1) Ms.Jaquline Moras, Daughter of
Late Mr.John Moras, aged 39 years, residing at
Taccode house and Post Karkala Taluk,
Mangalore District-574 197, and

2) Mrs.Malini Bakthaprasad, wife of
Mr.TBakthaprasad, aged 60 years, residing at
No.4 AC, 402, 4th main, 4th A Cross, OMBR
Layout, Bhuvanagiri, Bangalore-560 043, do
hereby solemnly affirm and state on oath as
follows:-

1. We submit that the Petitioner is the
Accused in CC.No.54217/2014 (Crime
No.14/2013), wherein Charge sheet was filed
by the Respondent No.1 for the offence
punishable underSections 341,504,323and506of the Indian Penal Code.

2. It is submitted that the complainant /
Respondent No.2, herein is none other than
the Mother-in-law of the Accused herein and
the complainant before the 1st Respondent
Police.

3. It is submitted that the Petitioner /
Accused, herein had filed a case bearing
No.MC-7/2011 under the provisions ofDomestic Violence Actagainst the husband
and the Father in law before the JMFC (III
Court) at Mangalore.

4. It is submitted that thereafter the
Complainant/Respondent No.2, the herein filed
a private complaint against the Accused /
Petitioner herein for the above aforesaid
offences and accordingly a charge sheet has
been filed.

5. It is submitted that this being the state
of affairs the husband of the complainant, the
Father in law of the Accused / Petitioner had14CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018filed a Writ Petition Nos.14529-14530/2015
challenging the orders passed in
M.C.No.07/2011 pending on the file of Hon'ble
JMFC (III Court).

6. It is submitted that during the pendency
of the said Writ Petition Nos.14529-

14530/2015, the matter was referred to the
Bangalore Mediation Centre to enable the
parties to arrive at a mutual settlement.
Accordingly, the parties in the Writ Petition
have amicably resolved their dispute and
entered into a Memorandum of Settlement
underSection 89of CPC before the Bangalore
Mediation Centre.

7. It is submitted that based on the said
Memorandum of Settlement this Hon'ble Court
disposed of the Writ Petition Nos.14529-
14530/2015 (GM-FC) and directed the registry
to dispatch the memorandum received from
the Bangalore Mediation centre to the I
Additional Principal Judge, Family Court,
Bengaluru, wherein M.C.No.2764/2012 was
pending.

8. It is submitted that the Son of the
Complainant / Respondent No.2 herein had
filed a Petition for Divorce underSection 10 (x)15CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018of theDivorce Actagainst his wife, the
Accused/petitioner herein in
M.C.No.2764/2012 on the file of the I
Additional Principal Judge Family Court at
Bangalore.

9. It is submitted that this Divorce Petition
was also referred to the Mediation Centre for
resolution of the dispute as per the directions
of this Hon'ble Court in W.P.Nos.14529-
14530/2015 and accordingly, the Parties to
the Divorce Petition namely B.Alwyn Jeetendar
and Jaquline Moras agreed to resolve their
dispute through the mediation process and
entered into a Memorandum of Settlement
underSection 89of CPC read with Rules 24
and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure
(Mediation) Rules 2005 in M.C.No.2764/2012.

10. It is submitted that based on the
Memorandum of Settlement executed by the
parties, the Hon'ble Family Court dissolved the
marriage between the parties therein and a
decree has been passed dissolving the said
marriage.

11. It is submitted that in both the
Memorandum of Settlement Agreement, the
parties have agreed to cooperate for16CRL.P No.458/2018c/w. CRL.P NO.1632/2018compounding the Criminal case
CC.No.54217/2014 filed before the X ACMM,
Bengaluru underSections 341,504,323and506of IPC.

12. It is respectfully submitted that the
whole set of cases both civil and criminal have
arisen from out of the marriage between the
husband and wife, which has been amicably
resolved and a Decree of divorce has been
granted by the I Additional Principal Judge
Family Court Bangalore, and the parties have
amicably agreed to compound the criminal
cases filed against each other to put an end to
the litigation.

13. It is respectfully submitted that no
purpose would be met by allowing the criminal
prosecution to continue in the above stated
case, as the parties have agreed to put an end
to the ill-fated litigation.

14. We submit that we have voluntarily
agreed to put an end to this litigation and
there is no force, coercion or under influence in
execution of this Joint Affidavit.

15. We submit that we have signed this
Affidavit out of free will and consent.

16. We pray that this Hon'ble Court may be
 pleased to allow the petition and Quash the
 proceedings in CC.No.54217/2014 on the
 file of the X Additional Chief Metropolitan
 Magistrate, Bangalore and consequently,
 Quash the crime No.14/2013 before the
 Ramamurthy Nagar Police Station, K.R.Puram
 Sub Division, Bangalore, in the interest of
 justice and equity." (sic)

5. The criminal proceedings underSection 498-Aof IPC have stemmed out of matrimonial dispute

between the parties. Parties have settled the

matrimonial dispute amicably. In the circumstances, it

is just and appropriate to quash the criminal

proceedings and accordingly all proceedings in

CC.No.23097/2012 and CC.No.54217/2014 both

pending on the file of X ACMM, Bengaluru, and the same

are accordingly, quashed.

6. Petitions are accordingly disposed of. No

costs.
Sd/-

JUDGE

Cs/-
